text:
maria: quick question — our debug cache (redis snapshot shards) sometimes stores request_id and trace ids. retention policy currently 90d, but legal asked whether we should prune customer-identifiable traces earlier for EU customers. do we have a short-term fix?

alek: short answer: we should avoid storing full trace payloads longer than 30d for EU by default. long answer: need approval from legal for automated deletion windows >30d. also depends on whether request_id maps to PII.

ryan: infra note: redis snapshots are global right now. we can add a lifecycle job to scrub keys with prefix `trace:` for customers with eu_tenant=true. low-risk change, I can draft a rake task.

maria: thanks. can you outline the minimal change? we need something we can ship this week to reduce exposure.

ryan: minimal: 1) add tag on tenant metadata (eu_tenant). 2) nightly job runs `SCAN` + `DEL` for `trace:eu:<tenant_id>:*` older than 30d. 3) emit metric `trace_prune.count`. sample pseudo:

```
# nightly prune
keys = redis.scan(match: "trace:eu:*")
keys.each do |k|
  if redis.ttl(k) == -1 && key_age(k) > 30.days
    redis.del(k)
  end
end
```

sana: legal: we are okay with a 30d default for EU tenants for debug snapshots, as long as: 1) we document the deletion behavior in the DPA annex, 2) customers can request full purge earlier via support, and 3) we retain an audit log of the deletion job (no payload, just keys deleted & tenant id). please coordinate the doc update with product.

anna: product: noted. will add to the privacy section of the docs. question: some enterprise customers asked for 180d retention for auditability — can we support exceptions?

alek: exceptions are fine but must be documented and approved by legal + security. for exceptions, we should store masked traces (hashed request ids, no payload) instead of raw. that reduces PII risk.

maria: so plan: roll nightly prune for any tenant with eu_tenant flag to 30d, add audit events to SQS (no payload), legal to update DPA, product to add opt-out/exception flow. ryan/infra to draft PR for prune job and opt-in metadata. can we get a short blameless runbook for failures?

ryan: i'll open a PR today, include a small runbook snippet: retry logic, metric thresholds (>5% of keys deleted triggers page), and S3 backup of audit events for 365d.

sana: legal will draft the DPA paragraph and loop in privacy counsel. we approve the 30d default with audit log retention as infra suggested.

anna: I'll add a doc stub and customer-facing FAQ. tagging @support for manual early purge requests.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: branch `eu-trace-prune` -> staging at 02:30 UTC. CI checks passed. :shipit:

maria: awesome — thanks everyone. filing a follow-up to track PR + DPA language.

alek: small follow-up: please ensure any logs that index request_id->user are redacted in the ELK pipeline too — we should treat trace deletion as part of a wider redaction pass.

ryan: noted, will add a grep-and-redact step in the log-shipper config and include it in the PR.

maria: perfect. closing the thread, ping if blockers show up.
